title: Instrumentation: add/verify normalized route tag on metering events at ingestion
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Usage Insights requires a stable `route` dimension for cost attribution by API route + model. Today a non-trivial subset of metering events arrive without a reliable route tag (notably streaming endpoints and some OpenAI-compat paths), which leads to “Unknown route” buckets and mismatches vs expectations.

This ticket adds/verified route tags in metering events at ingestion:
- Prefer emitted route fields from gateway when present.
- If missing, derive from request metadata available at ingestion (HTTP method + raw path), then normalize/canonicalize via the shared route normalization library.
- Record provenance (emitted vs derived) to support debugging and rollout.

This is intended to unblock accurate aggregations in ENG-3812 and reduce support issues like missing route breakdowns and unexplained “unknown route” spend.
acceptance_criteria:
- Metering events written to the warehouse include a stable, normalized route field suitable for rollups (e.g. `/v1/chat/completions`).
- For requests with path params, route is templated/canonicalized (no customer IDs, request IDs, or other high-cardinality leakage).
- Coverage: >= 99.5% of metering events for Hosted API include normalized route within 48h of rollout (excluding explicitly excluded/internal routes).
- Streaming (SSE) events in all regions populate the same normalized route as their non-streaming equivalents.
- OpenAI-compat endpoints map to the canonical Redwood route set (per ADR/ENG-3813 rules) so customers see consistent grouping.
- Provenance is recorded so we can audit how route was populated (emitted vs derived vs unknown).
- Monitoring is in place for unknown-route rate and cardinality regression (ties into ENG-3818 guardrails).
implementation_notes:
Fields:
- Add `metering.normalized_route` (string) as the canonical route dimension.
- Add `metering.route_source` (enum string): `emitted`, `derived_at_ingest`, `unknown`.
- Preserve existing raw fields (if present) for debugging only: `http.path` / `request_path` (do not use for aggregation).

Ingestion logic (high level):
1) If event already contains `route_template`/`http.route`/`api_route` from the gateway, run it through normalization library to ensure canonical formatting and mapping rules (idempotent).
2) Else, if event has `http.method` + `http.path` (or equivalent request metadata), derive a candidate route by applying the route normalization library in “derive” mode.
3) Else, set `metering.normalized_route = "unknown"` and `route_source = "unknown"`.

Normalization requirements:
- Must template common path params (workspace/project IDs, model IDs in path, etc.) and strip query params.
- Must apply OpenAI-compat mapping (e.g. `/v1/responses` vs `/v1/chat/completions`) to whichever canonical set we ship in Usage Insights.
- Must be consistent across regions and deployment modes, but this ticket scopes to Hosted API ingestion path; Dedicated/Private emitters follow in later work if needed.

Data/backfill:
- No historical backfill in this ticket. We will rely on forward fix + the separate backfill plan doc if needed.

Testing:
- Unit tests for known routes + edge cases (streaming endpoints, OpenAI-compat variants, trailing slashes).
- Property tests for “no high-cardinality” behavior (IDs don’t appear in normalized route).
- Sample replay of recent metering events to compute unknown-route % before/after.

Notes on compatibility:
- Do not break older emitters: treat missing route as expected; derive when possible.
- Keep any existing `route` fields unchanged for now (dual-write) to avoid breaking downstream consumers until aggregations are migrated.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement dual-write to `metering.normalized_route` + `metering.route_source` in ingestion, behind a server-side flag `metering_ingest_normalized_route_enabled`.
2) Canary enable in one low-traffic region for 24h.
3) Monitor:
   - % of events with `normalized_route != unknown`
   - Unique normalized route cardinality/day
   - Top 20 routes by volume to ensure mapping is sane
   - Streaming endpoint coverage specifically
4) Ramp to 50% regions, then all regions.
5) After stable for 72h, coordinate with ENG-3812/ENG-3814 to switch aggregations/queries to `metering.normalized_route`.

Rollback:
- Disable flag to revert to previous behavior (no normalized route derivation at ingest). Dual-written fields can remain but should be ignored by downstream until re-enabled.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: cardinality explosion if normalization misses an edge-case param. Mitigation: strict normalization + guardrail alerting (ENG-3818), plus automated check on daily unique route count.
- Risk: mapping changes alter customer-visible grouping. Mitigation: align with ADR and document canonical route set; track changes in a changelog and communicate in beta notes if needed.
- Risk: “unknown route” remains high for some pipelines (missing request metadata). Mitigation: identify missing metadata sources; if required, add gateway emission in follow-up ticket.
- Risk: discrepancy vs billing totals if route derivation drops events. Mitigation: no filtering; only populating additional tag; totals should be unaffected.

comments: 2026-01-29 (Logan Wright): Creating due to data audit finding: ~6–9% of Hosted API metering events missing route tag; biggest offender appears to be streaming chat in us-east + OpenAI-compat requests. Blocking accurate route/model rollups for beta.

2026-02-01 (Thomas Baird): Confirmed ingestion has method+path for most events even when route template missing. Proposing we derive normalized route at ingest using ENG-3813 library (once merged) and write `metering.normalized_route` + `route_source`.

2026-02-03 (Nadia Rahman): Please ensure normalized route never contains customer IDs. This is a cost attribution dimension and will end up in exports; treat as sensitive/high-visibility. Add a test that rejects UUID-like substrings and long numeric segments.

2026-02-05 (Thomas Baird): Implemented dual-write behind flag. Added sampling job to compute unknown-route % and top unknown examples (hashed raw path) for debugging without leaking raw path to dashboards.
2026-02-07 (Allison Grant): Ask: add an explicit metric `metering_unknown_route_rate` and alert if >1% for Hosted API for >30m during rollout. Also alert on route cardinality jump >20% day-over-day.

2026-02-09 (Thomas Baird): Canary enabled in eu-west. Unknown route dropped from 7.4% -> 0.6%. No cardinality spikes observed; top routes look correct. Noticed `/v1/chat/completions/` trailing slash variant showing up—added normalization to trim trailing slash except root.

2026-02-11 (Chloe Martin): Confirm this will cover OpenAI-compat endpoints. We saw support report that `/v1/chat/completions` calls via compat layer weren’t mapping to the same route grouping. Please validate with sample events.

2026-02-12 (Thomas Baird): Validated compat mapping on sample: `/openai/v1/chat/completions` now normalizes to `/v1/chat/completions` with `route_source=derived_at_ingest` when gateway doesn’t emit template. Streaming also consistent across regions in staging replay.
2026-02-14 (Thomas Baird): Rolled out to all regions at 50% traffic; holding here pending 24h observation + signoff from Allison (observability) and Nadia (attribution). Marking In Review.
